definitions.explanation: A white crystalline substance (sodium chloride) used for seasoning and preserving food. An essential cooking ingredient.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}を{少|すこ}し{入|い}れてください。
この{料理|りょうり}は{塩|しお}が{足|た}りません。
examples.english: This dish doesn't have enough salt.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}と{砂糖|さとう}を{間違|まちが}えました。
{塩|しお}は{体|からだ}に{必要|ひつよう}ですが、{取|と}りすぎはよくないです。
examples.english: Salt is necessary for the body, but taking too much is not good.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}の{水|みず}には{塩|しお}がたくさん{入|はい}っているので、{飲|の}むことができません。
examples.english: Seawater has a lot of salt in it, so you can't drink it.

notes:
{塩|しお} is salt, one of the most fundamental seasonings in Japanese cooking.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {塩|しお}を{入|い}れる: to add salt
- {塩加減|しおかげん}: salt seasoning (the right amount of salt)
- {塩味|しおあじ}: salty flavor
- {塩焼|しおや}き: salt-grilled (fish, etc.)
- {塩|しお}{漬|づ}け: salted/pickled

RELATED ADJECTIVE:
{塩辛|しおから}い or しょっぱい: salty (taste)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Salt has spiritual significance in Shinto. {清|きよ}めの{塩|しお} (purifying salt) is scattered at funerals and sumo matches. Small piles of {盛|も}り{塩|じお} are placed at shop entrances for good luck.

CONTRAST:
- {塩|しお}: salt
- {砂糖|さとう}: sugar
